messages:
elaine: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight 'degradation adapter' between the router and serving pools to enable graceful partial fallback without a full model swap. Sketch attached below.

sam_k: Curious — how is this different from current fallback policies? sounds like an intermediate path?

elaine: Exactly. Current fallbacks are 'hard' (swap model variant or route to different pool). Adapter lets us apply cheaper degradations in-line: token-sampling reduction, lower-precision variant, partial-response heuristics, or cached-prefix-only mode.

vijay: OK. Main concerns: session affinity + KV cache correctness when we flip modes mid-session. We can't invalidate client-visible continuity.

marco: Also: what signals drive it? latency percentiles? tail latency spikes? downstream error rates? Need an SLO->action mapping.

elaine: Proposal: adapter exposes a small interface to the router: evaluate(request_meta, current_metrics) -> DegradationPlan. Router queries adapter per-request when certain predicates match. Adapter decisions are per-tenant & per-route, with an ephemeral plan id.

elaine: Example plan schema (pseudo):
```
plan = {
  "id": "plan-2026-03-21-1",
  "mode": "kv_prefix_only|quant8_proxy|truncated_stream|suppress_tool_calls",
  "duration_ms": 15000,
  "fallback_weight": 0.3,
  "safety": { "min_quality_score": 0.75, "max_tokens": 128 },
  "signals": ["p99_latency>500ms", "error_rate>2%"]
}
```

sam_k: Where is state kept? adapter should be centralized for policy consistency or local for speed? tradeoffs: centralized = single source of truth for plans, but latency to check. local = faster but replication complexity.

elaine: Thinking hybrid: central control plane computes population-level plans and pushes compact signatures to local adapters (in the router layer). Local adapter can make per-request micro-decisions using local telemetry + pushed rules.

vijay: For KV-caching: adapter must tag responses with cache hints and maintain a session-compatibility token so subsequent requests can detect degraded-prefix dependencies. We'll need a compatibility-check API in the session store.

marco: Observability: each plan emits metrics: plan_applied, plan_reverted, quality_regression_{route,tenant}, effective_latency_saved. We'll wire those into the rollouts dashboard and the canary decision surface.

elaine: Rollout mechanics: 3-stage path: 1) dry-run (record-only) 2) soft-apply (adapter returns plan but router keeps original path unless forced by a throttle knob) 3) hard-apply (router honors plan). Transitions gated by signal windows and safety checks.

sam_k: How do we avoid oscillation across routes? e.g., bouncing plan on/off every minute.

elaine: Add hysteresis and cooldown: min_apply_time + exponential backoff. Also require multiple-window agreement (e.g., p99 high for 3/5 windows) before hard-apply.

marco: Integration with existing canary/A-B: adapter should be aware of traffic-split buckets so it doesn't silently bias a canary's exposure. Plans must be scoped to variants/buckets.

vijay: Security/compliance: plans contain no data, but ensure control-plane pushes are authenticated and auditable. Key rotation and audit log entries for plan pushes.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolling update started for router-adapter-service v0.3.0 — 6 pods -> 6 pods, env=staging

ops-bot: Note: spike detected on staging p99 after deploy, tagging this thread.

elaine: Good catch — we'll keep staging dry-run for now and validate quality metrics (rouge/accept-rate) on sample prompts before promoting.

sam_k: Action items: 1) small spike to implement plan schema + local adapter stub (sam) 2) session compatibility API proposal (vijay) 3) add metrics contract to console (marco) 4) short RFC doc for eng-architecture (elaine). I'll file the ticket and assign. :thumbsup:

elaine: Ty. I'll paste a minimal RFC link when it's up.
